findings.text: Execution-guard leak: executePodcastCron returns at line 214 before the cleanup filter at 218 and has no try/finally around the runEpisodeCheck loop — any throw leaks the guard and the same cron expression is permanently skipped ('only a warn is logged, downloads never run again until restart').

Library scan crons never torn down on library deletion: removeCronForLibrary only filters the array, never calls task.stop(), and LibraryController.delete never calls updateLibraryScanCron — deleted library's cron fires and logs 'Library not found' on every tick until restart.

handleAuthorCache is a near copy-paste of handleCoverCache with a behavior divergence: cover path supports global.XAccel redirect (57-61, 83-86) while author path silently lacks it; both use raw console.log(err) instead of Logger and `var` declarations.
reset() calls init() which re-registers all seven Sequelize hooks — every applied backup accumulates duplicate hook registrations, unbounded growth.

backupSqliteDb calls step(-1)/finish() unawaited then polls backup.completed/failed in a 500ms loop capped at ~2min — documented workaround for missing promised backup API; timeout rejects a string, not an Error.
Sentinel string coercion in client-facing payload: backupCount: totalBackupCount || 'Invalid', removedOldest: removedOldest || 'false' (boolean coerced to string).
Contract mismatch on onError callback: outer catch calls onError(error.message) (1 arg) while consumer SocketAuthority.js:415 expects (provider, errorMessage) — latent wire-shape bug.

OPML import: {taskTitleStringFeed, taskDescription, taskErrorString} triple repeated verbatim four times; getOPMLFeeds silently drops feeds whose getPodcastFeed fails (partial import, no error surfaced).
